observations: The trailing unterminated line is appended to out by the refill path but the call returns False: a while (ReadLine(...)) loop never sees it as a line. This is the one behaviour a naive line reader gets wrong, and the model reproduces it exactly.

A file ending exactly on an 8192-byte boundary does not set at_eof_ on the full read; EOF is learned only from the next call's zero-byte refill Read. The model reproduces this: at_eof_ is set only when result.size() != 8192.
The IOSTATS bytes-read add precedes the status check, so a failed Read still adds its (partial) result size to the TLS counter. The model records the add on both paths.

The entry gate leaves out untouched on a sticky error, but out IS cleared before the loop on a healthy call -- so a partial line left in out by a failed call survives into the caller's hands only when the caller reuses the same string, which Parse does not (it breaks the loop on False).
MustCheck() has no binary call: it is an empty inline in this build, compiled out on all three false-return paths (entry gate, at_eof_, read error).

The binary's IOStatus move copies bytes 0-1, 3-4, 5 and 8-15 and leaves byte 2 and bytes 6-7 untouched; the second operator delete[] at 0x60d4e2b is dead (its argument was just zeroed). Both are recorded, not modelled as live behaviour.
The two TLS-helper calls (0x606d9f0) carry no sync-point string, so no upstream sync-point name is pinned for them; they are the IOSTATS_ADD expansion, not TEST_SYNC_POINT calls.

The constructor is a forwarding template with an empty body; buf_begin_/buf_end_ start at buf_.data() by their default member initialisers -- so the first ReadLine call always refills (remaining = 0). The model initialises pos_ == end_ == 0 for the same reason.
No /home/ paths appear in the packet excerpts: the objdump excerpt uses the repo-relative binary path work/hl-node-115.bin (the #5857 defect class, avoided).
